about: The review of each map's exact bytes (docs/decisions/0017-a-map-change-carries-a-review-of-its-bytes.md). tools/check-map-review.py fails any map whose sha256 is not the one recorded here.

corpus-map.json.note: #125 (the engine's finding 18) added a second part to two ambiguity questions: must-play-whole-throw's asks whether two orders of a throw reaching the same position are one play or two, and bearing-off-eligible's whether bearing off can begin partway through the throw that brings the last man home. The notes of both, of move-by-pip and of bearing-off-move-or-remove were changed to match, citing the blind-mapping rows move-by-pip|clarity|die-movement (stands) and move-by-pip|suspendedBy|die-movement (read as not deciding the mid-throw case). No clarity, fate, evidence or edge changed. It is a semantic change, so it carries an independent verdict and not an exemption. The verdict file names these bytes and records two rounds. previousReview is the review of the map #117 and #118 left (previousSha256), unchanged.

previousReview.note: #117 and #118 (docs/decisions/0025) added assertedBy to agreed-backgammon-multiple (caller, with the reason in its note, and the note's 'in the players' softened) and draws to opening-roll and throw-two-dice. No other entry changed. It is a semantic change, so it carries an independent verdict and not an exemption. The verdict file names these bytes and records two rounds. previousReview is the review of the map #102 left (previousSha256), unchanged.

#102 (the engine's finding 17) corrected game-value's ambiguity question to name both cases where the gammon and backgammon conditions overlap, a man up and a man in the winner's home table with nothing borne off; narrowed its gap case to a man outside both home tables; and added to its note both overlap cases as demonstrations and why 'begun to bear off' means removal. No other entry changed. It is a semantic change, so it carries an independent verdict and not an exemption. The verdict file names these bytes and records three rounds. previousReview is the blind-second-mapping review of the map #95 left (previousSha256), unchanged.

Issue #95. compare.py read the map at 32c5a69 (32 entries), the bytes the legacy exemption covered, and exits 1 unless each of its 127 flags has a row in resolutions.json. The map was corrected to those rows (18 blind-right, 5 corpus-does-not-settle; 33 entries) in the same commit that replaced the exemption with this review. sha256 is the corrected map; compared.sha256 is the map before correction. The blind mapper worked from docs with every backgammon example removed (blind-mapping/REDACTIONS.md); what could not be ruled out is in blind-mapping/README.md, Limits.
